definition: Electrochemical dualism is an [obsolete scientific theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obsolete_scientific_theory) in [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) relevant between around 1800 and around 1830 and pioneered by [Jöns Jacob Berzelius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jöns_Jacob_Berzelius).

Electrochemical engineering is the branch of [chemical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_engineering) dealing with the technological applications of [electrochemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrochemistry) phenomena, such as [electrosynthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrosynthesis) of chemicals, [electrowinning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrowinning) and refining of metals, [flow batteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_battery) and [fuel cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuel_cells), surface modification by electrodeposition, electrochemical separations and [corrosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrosion).

electrochemical equivalent (Eq or Z) of a [chemical element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_element) is the [mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass) of that element (in [gram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram)s) transported by a specific quantity of electricity, usually expressed in grams per [coulomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulomb) of [electric charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_charge).

Electrochemistry is the branch of [physical chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_chemistry) concerned with the relationship between [electrical potential difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_potential) and identifiable [chemical change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_change).

Electrodeionization (EDI) is a water treatment technology that utilizes [DC power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_current), [ion exchange membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion-exchange_membrane), and [ion exchange resin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_exchange_resin) to [deionize water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purified_water), thereby removing [trace mineral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trace_mineral)s that function as [anions and cations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anions_and_cations).

Electrodialysis (ED) is used to transport [salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt) [ions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ions) from one [solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_(chemistry)) through [ion-exchange membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion-exchange_membrane)s to another solution under the influence of an applied [electric potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_potential) difference.

Electrodiffusiophoresis is a motion of particles dispersed in liquid induced by external homogeneous [electric field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_field), which makes it similar to [electrophoresis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrophoresis).

electrofuge is a [leaving group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaving_group) that does not retain the [lone pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lone_pair) of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s from its previous [bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covalent_bond) with another species (in contrast to a [nucleofuge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleofuge), which does).

Electrokinetic phenomena are a family of several different effects that occur in [heterogeneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterogeneous) [fluids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluids), or in porous bodies filled with fluid, or in a fast flow over a flat surface.

electrolyte is a substance that conducts [electricity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electricity) through the movement of [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion)s, but not through the movement of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s.
electrolytic process is the use of [electrolysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrolysis) industrially to refine metals or compounds at a high purity and low cost.

electromeric effect is a molecular [polarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_polarity) occurring by an intramolecular [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) displacement, characterized by the substitution of one [electron pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_pair) for another within the same [atomic octet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octet_rule) of electrons.
Electrometallurgy is a method in [metallurgy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallurgy) that uses electrical energy to produce metals by electrolysis.

definition: electron configuration is the [distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_(mathematics)) of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s of an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) (or other physical structure) in [atomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital) or [molecular orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_orbital)s.
electron counting is a formalism for assigning a number of [valence electrons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence_electrons) to individual atoms in a molecule.

electron deficiency (and electron-deficient) is jargon that is used in two contexts: chemical species that violate the [octet rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octet_rule) because they have too few valence electrons and species that happen to follow the octet rule but have electron-acceptor properties, forming donor-acceptor [charge-transfer salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge-transfer_salt)s.

electron hole (often simply called a hole) is a [quasiparticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasiparticle) denoting the lack of an electron at a position where one could exist in an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or [atomic lattice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_structure).

Electron-rich is jargon that is used in multiple related meanings with either or both kinetic and thermodynamic implications: * with regard to [electron-transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron-transfer), electron-rich species have low [ionization energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionization_energy) and/or are [reducing agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reducing_agent).
electron-withdrawing group (EWG) is a [group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_group) or atom that has the ability to draw electron density toward itself and away from other adjacent atoms.

electric effect influences the [structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_structure), [reactivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactivity_(chemistry)), or [properties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_properties) of a [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) but is neither a traditional [bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_bond) nor a [steric effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steric_effect).

electronvolt (symbol eV), also written as electron-volt and electron volt, is a [unit of measurement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_measurement) equivalent to the amount of [kinetic energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinetic_energy) gained by a single [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) accelerating through an [electric potential difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltage) of one [volt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volt) in a [vacuum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum).

hydroformylation, also known as oxo synthesis or oxo process, is an industrial process for the production of [aldehyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldehyde)s () from [alkene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkene)s ().

Hydrogen isotope [biogeochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogeochemistry) (HIBGC) is the scientific study of biological, geological, and chemical processes in the environment using the distribution and relative abundance of [hydrogen isotopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_isotopes).

Hydrogen pinch analysis (HPA) is a [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) management method that originates from the concept of heat [pinch analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinch_analysis).
Hydrogen purification is any technology used to purify [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen).

Hydrogen-bond catalysis is a type of [organocatalysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organocatalysis) that relies on use of [hydrogen bonding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_bonding) interactions to accelerate and control [organic reactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_reactions).

Hydrogenography is a combinatorial method based on the observation of [optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical) changes on the metal surface by [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) [absorption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_(chemistry)).

Hydrogen–deuterium exchange (also called H–D or H/D exchange) is a [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction) in which a covalently bonded [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) atom is replaced by a [deuterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deuterium) atom, or vice versa.

hydrological transport model is a [mathematical model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model) used to simulate the flow of rivers, [streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream_flow), groundwater movement or [drainage front displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffman–Taylor_instability), and calculate [water quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_quality) parameters.
Hydrolysis (; ) is any [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction) in which a molecule of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) breaks one or more chemical bonds.

Hydrolyzed vegetable protein (HVP) products are foodstuffs obtained by the [hydrolysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrolysis) of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), and have a [meaty, savory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umami) taste similar to [broth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broth) (bouillon).

Hydrometalation (hydrometallation) is a type of [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction) in [organometallic chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organometallic_chemistry) in which a [chemical compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_compound) with a [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) to [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal) bond (M-H, metal [hydride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydride)) adds to compounds with an [unsaturated bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturated_and_unsaturated_compounds) like an [alkene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkene) (RC=CR) forming a new compound with a [carbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon) to metal bond (RHC-CRM).

definition: Medication (also called medicament, medicine, pharmaceutical drug, medicinal product, medicinal drug, or simply drug) is a [drug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug) used to [diagnose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_diagnosis), [cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cure), treat, or [prevent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preventive_medicine) disease.

Medicinal or pharmaceutical chemistry is a scientific discipline at the intersection of [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) and [pharmacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacy) involved with [designing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_design) and developing [pharmaceutical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical) [drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medication).

Medicinal Chemistry Research is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [medicinal chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicinal_chemistry) emphasizing the structure-activity relationships of biologically active compounds.

Medicinal Research Reviews is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that publishes reviews on topics related to medicinal research.

Medicines Discovery Catapult (MDC) is the United Kingdom's [catapult centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catapult_centres) for medicine research and innovation, headquartered at [Alderley Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderley_Park) in [Cheshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire).

microreactor or microstructured reactor or microchannel reactor is a device in which [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction)s take place in a confinement with typical lateral dimensions below 1 kg at a moderate number of experiments per day (3-15).

Microscale chemistry (often referred to as small-scale chemistry, in German: [[:de:Chemie im Mikromaßstab|Chemie im Mikromaßstab]]) is an [analytical method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytical_chemistry) and also a [teaching method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teaching_method) widely used at [school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School) and at [university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University) levels, working with small quantities of [chemical substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance)s.

microscopic reversibility in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) and [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) is twofold: * First, it states that the microscopic detailed dynamics of particles and fields is time-reversible because the microscopic equations of motion are symmetric with respect to inversion in time ([T-symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-symmetry)); * Second, it relates to the statistical description of the kinetics of macroscopic or mesoscopic systems as an ensemble of elementary processes: collisions, elementary transitions or reactions.
Microsegregation is a non-uniform chemical separation and concentration of elements or impurities in [alloys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alloys) after they have solidified.
Microwave Active Composition is a brand of [microwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microwave)-sensitive liquid chemicals sold by Atlanta Chemical Engineering LLC.

reactive center, also called a propagating center, in [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry) is a particular location, usually an atom, within a chemical compound that is the likely center of a reaction in which the chemical is involved.

reactive empirical bond-order (REBO) model is a function for calculating the [potential energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_energy) of [covalent bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covalent_bonds) and the [interatomic force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interatomic_force).

reactivity is the impulse for which a [chemical substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance) undergoes a [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction), either by itself or with other materials, with an overall release of [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy).

definition: β-Carbon elimination (beta-carbon elimination) is a type of reaction in [organometallic chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organometallic_chemistry) wherein an [allyl ligand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allyl_ligand) bonded to a metal center is broken into the corresponding [metal-bonded alkyl (aryl)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aryl) ligand and an [alkene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkene).

β-Hydride elimination is a reaction in which a metal-[alkyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkyl) centre is converted into the corresponding metal-[hydride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydride)-[alkene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkene).
